summary.text: A 57-year-old African American man with congestive heart failure, an implantable defibrillator, type 2 diabetes, stroke, coronary artery disease, sleep apnea, hypertension, chronic kidney disease of unknown stage and gout presented on 14 May 2020 with worsening shortness of breath and chest pain. Baseline testing showed a left ventricular ejection fraction of 20%, creatinine 5.08 mg/dL, eGFR 14 and carbon dioxide 18 mmol/L, and he was on 11 prescription medications.

He initially declined hospitalization and started a defined plant-based diet with a reduced diuretic dose. After four days his angina and breathing difficulty had resolved and several medications were stopped; by day 7 he had black stool, lightheadedness, recurrent shortness of breath and a blood pressure of 69/41 mmHg, received 2000 mL of saline, and had Eliquis and torsemide stopped. On day 8 creatinine was 12.10 mg/dL, eGFR 4 and carbon dioxide 11 mmol/L, and he was hospitalized.

On admission he was severely acidotic with an arterial blood gas pH of 7.12. Milrinone was stopped for worsening tachycardia, and a nuclear stress test showed an anterior and apical non-transmural scar with an ejection fraction below 20%. Intravenous sodium bicarbonate in 0.45% sodium chloride was infused at 100 mL/h with 6 L of fluids during the stay, his acidosis began clearing within hours, and he continued the diet in hospital.

He was discharged on 28 May 2020 on two medications and was free of lightheadedness, weakness, chest pain and shortness of breath. At follow-up his treadmill exercise time rose from 4 min 18 s to 13 min 3 s, the frequent premature ventricular complexes were no longer present, and on 11 June 2020 creatinine was 1.8 mg/dL and eGFR 47 with an 82% decrease in medications.
